FU-001.reason: The native server (12306) replaces @fastify/cors (origin: true) with ncore's shared K7 guard (local_rpc_guard.createFastifyGuard, onRequest + preParsing), so there is no second implementation; the own request-guard.ts is deleted. Options: allowedOrigins = the fixed EXTENSION_ID origin plus the launching extension origin from the browser argv (validated as chrome-extension://[a-p]{32}), and allowLoopbackOrigins false. Result: a loopback peer with a loopback Host and either no Origin (local MCP clients, the next native host) or the extension origin is allowed; any other web origin, and any DNS-rebinding Host, falls to K3 and is refused, including the /singleton shutdown. CORS reflects only the extension origin.

issues: (non-blocking) native-server/package.json still lists @fastify/cors, now unused; left in place to avoid an unrequested install/lockfile change.

(note) The native host now loads ncore modules from the repository (ncore.ts with REPO_ROOT, same depth for src and dist) and sets MCP_MODE=mcp first so ncore logs go to stderr, not the native-messaging stdout. It therefore needs the repository checkout, the same assumption the existing constant/index.ts already makes for config/service_contract.

(resubmission) the Chrome extension id has one definition, service_contract.json#mcp_chrome.extension_id, exported by packages/shared (EXTENSION_ID) and re-exported by native-server scripts/constant.ts; native-host-common.cjs and update-extension-id.cjs read it. The guard options use it.
